subject: Post-call: Competitive evaluation lab scope & next experiments (tool-calling / streaming)
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@skyward.ai>, Tim Rocha <tim@cloudbench.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Competitive evaluation lab scope & next experiments (tool-calling / streaming)

Hi Alyssa / Tim —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed scope so we can align the lab work around the specific parity checks you care about. I tried to keep this tight and actionable.

Key takeaways from our call:
- Skyward’s priorities: 1) deterministic tool/function calling (low false positives on invocation), 2) structured JSON outputs for downstream ingestion, 3) sub-300ms cold-start and steady-state streaming for short responses (<=80 tokens).
- Your current baselines: CloudBench endpoints for generation + an in-house router to split traffic across model variants. You called out higher tail latency and occasional function misfires when prompts are slightly ambiguous.
- Success criteria for our side-by-side: false-invocation rate <= 2% on your tool test set; valid-JSON parse rate >= 98% on structured-output eval; median streaming TTFB < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for your traffic profile.

Proposed lab experiments (attached as rdw-parity-test-plan.md and a CSV with the initial test vectors):
1) Tool/function-calling: run the Skyward function set (50 functions) against 1k prompts with ambiguity perturbations (we'll run on both Redwood hosted and CloudBench for parity).
   - Metric: invocation precision/recall, confidence threshold ROC
2) Structured outputs: golden JSON schema tests (200 records) + fuzzing inputs to measure parser failures and schema drift.
   - Metric: parse success rate, schema validation errors
3) Streaming perf: continuous 30-min traffic replay at your P95 QPS for short responses and a separate long-response profile.
   - Metric: median TTFB, p95/p99 latency, rebuffer events, cost-per-token estimate
4) Fallback/bandwidth tests: induce a simulated capacity constraint to validate graceful degradation (model fallback and truncated streaming behavior).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the Skyward test vectors + share a redacted sample (1-2 examples per function).
- We run a quick smoke run (2 hours) on Redwood hosted and share results within 48 hours.
- If smoke looks good, we schedule a 3-day focused lab and invite your engineers for a joint session to review failures.

I attached a short CSV for you to drop samples into and a formal test plan. Laura and Steph are looped for sequencing and to scope any reserved Dedicated capacity if we need it.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
Attachments: rdw-parity-test-plan.md (text), redwood_lab-scope.csv (csv)
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@skyward.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, Tim Rocha <tim@cloudbench.io>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive evaluation lab scope & next experiments (tool-calling / streaming)

Thanks Karthik — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before we drop the sample set: 

1) For tool invocation metrics: when you say precision/recall, can you confirm you’ll surface both nominal invocation (trigger/no-trigger) and the argument extraction quality? The latter is critical because we pipeline the args to workflows.
2) For streaming: our short responses are typically 20–60 tokens; long responses (system summaries) are 200–400 tokens. The 30-min replay can be shared as a HAR file — I’ll have Tim send that over.
3) Fallback behavior: we want to observe how Redwood behaves if model A fails (e.g., OOM) — does the system retry behind the scenes or return best-effort partial streams?

We’ll upload a redacted sample set to the Drive link you shared. Expect the first drop (50 tool prompts, 100 json-schema golden pairs) by EOD Monday.

Also looping Tim from CloudBench — Tim, thanks for offering to stand up the CloudBench baseline with our current config. Can you confirm the endpoint URL and auth method you’ll use so we can include it in the test harness?

Best,
Alyssa
Head of ML Platform | Skyward AI
From: Tim Rocha <tim@cloudbench.io>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@skyward.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive evaluation lab scope & next experiments (tool-calling / streaming)

Quick note — CloudBench will expose a temporary test endpoint (api.cloudbench.io/skyward-test) using API key auth. We’ll provide the key in a secure snippet and rotate after the lab. We’ll mirror the same sampling traffic you share.

I’ll coordinate with Alyssa on the HAR and the exact QPS profile. Looking forward to seeing the rdw results.

—Tim
CTO | CloudBench
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive evaluation lab scope & next experiments (tool-calling / streaming)

Alyssa / Tim — appreciate the quick turn. Two operational notes from our side as we prep: 

1) Data handling & redaction: please use the Drive upload and mark files as "redacted" if they contain PII. We will only mount the files into an ephemeral lab environment (no logging of raw inputs outside the test run).
2) Reserved capacity: based on the profiles you shared on the call, we recommend a small Dedicated pool for the 3-day lab window to avoid noisy neighbor interference. Steph, please prepare an estimate and a short approval note for Skyward.

Steph — can you draft the Dedicated quote and include burst policy (x2 QPS for 1 hour) and a failover to Redwood-hosted instances if we detect capacity constraints?

I’ll run the initial smoke tomorrow afternoon and post results to the Drive link and HubSpot (HSK-987654).

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
